newsitem.title: CHAD: Niger, FARS rebels agree ceasefire at talks in Chad.
newsitem.headline: Niger, FARS rebels agree ceasefire at talks in Chad.

text.p: The government of Niger and ethnic Toubou rebels have agreed a ceasefire after six days of talks in neighbouring Chad, a Chadian statement said on Friday.
The Revolutionary Armed Forces of the Sahara (FARS), led by Barka Wardougou, held talks in N'Djamena with a Nigerien government delegation led by Interior Minister Idi Ango Omar.

"At the end of their meetings, the two parties, convinced of the necessity of establishing total and definitive peace in Niger, agreed to observe a ceasefire with effect from 00h Niamey time on Tuesday June 10," the statement said.
It said the two sides would meet again in N'Djamena in three months to resume negotiations with the participation of "friendly countries" Algeria, France, Libya, Chad and Burkina Faso.
The FARS held Canadian aid worker Serge L'Archer and Mohamed Mallam, a soldier of Niger's Republican Guard, for three months before handing them over to Libya.
They were seized in the northern Kawar region on the Libyan border on February 27. Libya flew them to Niamey on May 22, after a visit to Niger by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi.
The FARS said it had taken them hostage to draw attention to its demand for autonomy for the Kawar region, and for an investigation into the death of 14 of its fighters in January.
Two Nigerien officials seized with them were released after a month following negotiations between the FARS and the government.
